active_themes.label: Warsh Faces First Test
active_themes.summary: A new wrinkle: the yen slid to its weakest level against the dollar in 40 years, and the US Treasury reportedly stepped in to support it — an unusual role reversal that signals officials see dollar strength as disorderly, not just a Japan problem. This adds a currency-stability dimension to the Fed-credibility test that was previously just about domestic rates and inflation prints.

active_themes.label: Markets Absorb The War
active_themes.summary: No escalation and no breakthrough today — stocks slipped modestly as investors watched ongoing Mideast talks alongside earnings, with oil holding near $80. The market is still pricing resolution rather than breakdown, which means the real risk remains a public collapse in talks, not another contained strike.

active_themes.label: Consumer Resilience Bounce
active_themes.summary: The pattern flipped from yesterday: instead of the Dow holding up while S&P and Nasdaq slipped, today the Dow underperformed by a wide margin while the other two indices were nearly flat. That's consistent with rate-sensitive sectors bearing the brunt of the mortgage-rate story while AI-driven tech names stay comparatively insulated — the open question is whether that rotation deepens or was just one day's noise.

active_themes.label: Credibility, Not Oil
active_themes.summary: Mortgage rates rising a fifth straight week to their highest point in over a year is fresh evidence the underlying yield pressure hasn't broken, even without a new 10-year Treasury print today. Meanwhile gold's rally into its best week since January is betting the opposite — that hike fears are overblown — so the credibility question (does the bond market or the gold market have it right) is now sharper, not resolved.

open_watchlist.condition: Shipping insurance premiums or transit delays through the Strait of Hormuz rise measurably following the weekend tanker strike.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would signal the war is starting to show up as a real cost in freight and insurance markets, not just a headline the market has learned to shrug off.

open_watchlist.condition: This week's jobs report shows payroll growth reaccelerating rather than confirming recent labor-market weakness.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would be the strongest confirmation yet that the GDP-fueled rally reflects real economic resilience rather than a one-time bounce.

open_watchlist.condition: The next CPI or PCE inflation print either echoes or contradicts today's four-year-high indicator reading.
open_watchlist.meaning: Validation would sharply raise the odds of a 2026 rate hike being seriously discussed; contradiction would let today's rally stand unchallenged.

open_watchlist.condition: US-Iran peace talks produce either a concrete framework or a public breakdown.
open_watchlist.meaning: A breakdown would hit markets harder than the recent tanker strike did, since today's rally just priced in the opposite outcome.

open_watchlist.condition: Israeli strikes on Lebanon draw a direct Iranian or Hezbollah response, rather than staying a contained strike-and-pause pattern.
open_watchlist.meaning: That would mean the market's decision to price talks over strikes today was premature, and the Mideast-optimism rally in the Dow is exposed.

open_watchlist.condition: Additional chip or megacap tech earnings guidance echoes the same spending-without-clear-return caution seen around AMD today.
open_watchlist.meaning: That would turn today's Nasdaq drag from an isolated story into confirmation of the broader AI-capex anxiety the market has been trying to ignore.

open_watchlist.condition: The yen falls through today's 40-year low against the dollar for a second consecutive session.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms a real trend rather than a one-day print, raising the odds of forced carry-trade unwinding that spills into US equities.

open_watchlist.condition: The US Treasury confirms direct dollar-selling intervention to support the yen.
open_watchlist.meaning: Signals officials view the dollar's strength as a systemic risk worth spending reserves on, not background noise.

open_watchlist.condition: Mortgage rates rise for a sixth consecutive week past today's one-year high.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms tightening credit is deepening, not plateauing, adding weight to the hawkish side of the Fed-credibility question.

open_watchlist.condition: Gold's weekly gain holds even as the 10-year Treasury yield resumes climbing.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would mean gold is being bought as a pure inflation hedge, not a rate-cut bet — a very different, more troubling signal for the Fed.
